topic: Gut microbiome dysbiosis and cardiovascular disease risk

themes: Microbiome composition shifts under metabolic stress
Systemic inflammation as a shared downstream pathway
Cardiovascular risk stratification via inflammatory markers
synth.consensus: Dysbiosis and elevated inflammatory markers are each independently associated with worse outcomes in their respective literatures.
synth.tensions: The microbiome literature and the cardiovascular-risk literature rarely cite each other directly; inflammation appears in both but is rarely treated as the connecting mechanism.
gaps: No study directly measures whether correcting dysbiosis changes cardiovascular risk markers
Cytokine-panel differences across dysbiosis subtypes are unreported
biases: Most cohorts are single-site, limiting generalizability

extractions.method: 16S rRNA sequencing of stool samples, n=142 metabolic-syndrome patients vs matched controls
extractions.finding: Dysbiosis (reduced Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio) correlates with lower short-chain fatty acid production and elevated serum IL-6.
extractions.limitation: No longitudinal follow-up; cannot establish causal direction
extractions.contribution: First to jointly quantify SCFA depletion and IL-6 elevation in the same dysbiotic cohort
extractions.excerpt: Reduced SCFA-producing taxa were associated with a 1.8x increase in circulating IL-6 (p<0.01).

extractions.method: Germ-free mouse colonization with dysbiotic vs healthy human donor microbiota
extractions.finding: Colonization with dysbiotic microbiota increased intestinal permeability and downstream innate immune activation.
extractions.data: Animal model, n=24 mice per arm
extractions.limitation: Mouse model may not translate directly to human immune signaling
extractions.contribution: Mechanistic evidence for a gut-barrier route from dysbiosis to systemic immune activation
extractions.excerpt: FITC-dextran permeability was 2.3x higher in dysbiotic-colonized mice (p<0.001).
extractions.relevance: Mechanistic link between dysbiosis and immune/inflammatory signaling

extractions.method: Prospective cohort, n=3,400, 8-year follow-up, serum inflammatory markers vs incident cardiovascular events
extractions.finding: Elevated IL-6 and CRP at baseline independently predicted incident atherosclerotic cardiovascular events.
extractions.metrics: Hazard ratio per SD increase in IL-6/CRP
extractions.limitation: Residual confounding from diet and physical activity not fully captured
extractions.contribution: Large prospective evidence tying systemic inflammation to cardiovascular outcomes
extractions.excerpt: Each SD increase in IL-6 was associated with a hazard ratio of 1.31 (95% CI 1.18-1.46) for incident cardiovascular events.

extractions.method: Case-control study of atherosclerotic plaque composition, n=210
extractions.finding: Plaques from patients with elevated systemic cytokines showed more unstable, lipid-rich cores than low-cytokine patients.
extractions.metrics: Plaque instability index, cytokine panel (IL-6, TNF-alpha, IL-1beta)
extractions.limitation: Cross-sectional; cannot show whether cytokines caused plaque instability or resulted from it
extractions.contribution: Links cytokine elevation to a specific structural cardiovascular risk marker (plaque instability), not just event incidence
extractions.excerpt: High-cytokine patients had a 2.1x higher plaque instability index (p=0.003).
extractions.relevance: Mechanistic detail on inflammation -> cardiovascular risk pathway
